angle_gap: Purely anecdotal personal-opinion piece from one content marketer on 'characteristics I like in a writer' — no structured way to evaluate those traits before hiring, no interview questions, no work-sample criteria; a hiring manager reading it still has no repeatable process to tell a curious, fresh-voiced writer from someone who interviews well but can't deliver.
asset: How to Evaluate a Copywriter's Storytelling and Range Before You Hire Them
distinct_angle: Turns the author's subjective checklist (curiosity, humor, storytelling) into a structured pre-hire evaluation — sample prompts and criteria a recruiter can actually score against, which the original never provides.

angle_gap: Leans on a single third-party stat set (attributed to 'Lever', undated in the visible text) and treats screening as a one-line touchpoint ('are candidates aware of the success criteria') without ever explaining how to make screening transparent or fair — no mention of structured, skills-based assessment as the mechanism for a better candidate experience at that stage.
asset: Fixing the Screening Stage of Candidate Experience with Transparent Skills Assessments
distinct_angle: Goes deep on the one stage (screening) the page treats as a throwaway bullet, showing how a transparent, skills-based process — not just 'good communication' — is what actually improves candidate experience there.

angle_gap: Thin, promo-driven recruitment guide: a bullet list of duties and one vague 'Skills needed' paragraph, then pivots straight into a CTA to sign up for their assessment library — no actual interview questions, no breakdown of which skills to test for and how, no worked example of evaluating a candidate.
asset: How to Hire a Warehouse Manager Who Can Actually Run the Floor, Not Just Talk About It
distinct_angle: Replaces the vague 'skills needed' paragraph and sales pivot with concrete, testable competencies (inventory systems, staff scheduling, safety compliance) and sample interview questions tied to each — the depth this page skips in favor of a signup CTA.

angle_gap: Skills testing is raised as step one but never developed — 'customize a skills test with real-world tasks' is a single sentence with no guidance on what to test, how to weight it against the referral relationship, or how to keep the process consistent across referred vs. non-referred candidates; the piece then drifts into group interviews and reference checks without tying back to the skills-based framing it opened with.
asset: Building a Skills-Based Vetting Process That Treats Referrals Like Every Other Candidate
distinct_angle: Develops the one-line 'customize a skills test' suggestion into an actual framework — what to test, how to score it identically for referred and non-referred candidates — closing the gap this page opens and abandons.
